{"summary": "Implemented odd_Days(N) as the number of days beyond complete weeks in N Gregorian years, and added tests covering the example, leap years, and century cycles.", "files": {"solution.py": """"Write a python function to calculate the number of odd days in a given year."""


def odd_Days(N):
    """Write a python function to calculate the number of odd days in a given year.

    Odd days are the days remaining after complete weeks are removed.
    An ordinary year contributes 1 odd day (365 % 7) and a leap year
    contributes 2 odd days (366 % 7), so for ``N`` years the total is
    ``N + leap_years`` modulo 7. Leap years are counted with the
    Gregorian rule: divisible by 4, except century years unless they
    are divisible by 400 (e.g. 100 years contain 24 leap years, giving
    (100 + 24) % 7 == 5 odd days).
    """
    leap_years = N // 4 - N // 100 + N // 400
    return (N + leap_years) % 7

    # 3 ordinary years and 1 leap year: 3 * 1 + 2 == 5 odd days.
    assert solution.odd_Days(4) == 5
    assert solution.odd_Days(5) == 6
    assert solution.odd_Days(6) == 0
    assert solution.odd_Days(7) == 1

def test_century_cycle():
    assert solution.odd_Days(100) == 5
    assert solution.odd_Days(200) == 3
    assert solution.odd_Days(300) == 1
    # A 400-year Gregorian cycle contains a whole number of weeks.
    assert solution.odd_Days(400) == 0
    assert solution.odd_Days(500) == 5
    assert solution.odd_Days(800) == 0


def test_after_400_year_cycle():
    assert solution.odd_Days(401) == 1
    assert solution.odd_Days(404) == 5

        assert 0 <= solution.odd_Days(years) < 7
